cohort: The study included singleton infants born in the state of New Jersey from 1996 to 2006, specifically comparing those born late-preterm (34-36 weeks) to full-term (37-41 weeks).
finding: Late-preterm birth increased the odds of a neonatal respiratory condition by more than fourfold and neonatal hyperbilirubinemia by more than fivefold, even when comparing births to the same mother and controlling for various demographic, economic, behavioral, and obstetric factors.
